Neither agent was measured for time or cost; the Claude rounds were no slower than Codex's and failed more on the shape of the draft than on speed, which this spec addresses.
149	- Measured at the end of this spec: Claude Code offers an operating-system sandbox of its own (`sandbox.enabled` in the settings, which a profile can pass with `--settings`), built on bubblewrap and socat. `bwrap` is installed on this machine and `socat` is not: with the sandbox enabled and `socat` missing, the CLI reports "Sandbox disabled: dependencies are missing" and runs the commands unsandboxed, so enabling it without the dependency would claim a guarantee that is not enforced. Equivalence with Codex therefore needs `socat` installed and a Claude profile that passes the sandbox settings, checked at launch.

153	## 7. Final Report
154	
155	### Delivered scope
156	The brief of `review-brief/7` states twelve rules (the tenth, the identifiers of prior findings, in review-brief/5; the eleventh group, the accepted-risk severities, the deferred tool, the component scoping, the mapping basis and the decision line, in review-brief/6) the engine checks on a typed conclusion and that a draft breaking one is refused whole (R1); a test ties each preflight blocker to the sentence of the brief that states its rule (R2); `review-brief/3` still renders as before and runs briefed with it conclude (R3); the Claude reviewer profile allows read-only commands in all three of its commands (R4); the manual names the template (R5). Left out: validating a draft before the run ends, and a change to any rule of the preflight.
157	
158	### Files and modules changed
159	- pose-mcp/internal/pose (review_brief.go, review_conclusions.go and their tests)
160	- .pose/policy/delegation.json (the Claude reviewer profile)
161	- POSE.md and its pt-BR and scaffold copies; the validation matrix gains `review-brief-conclusion-rules-integration`
162	
163	### Validation executed
164	- Command: `pose validate --strict --jobs 4` on a clean clone of the reviewed head, and the suites of `internal/pose`, `internal/cli` and `internal/mcpserver`
165	- Result: recorded by the sealed validation evidence; independent delegated review by a different agent, concluded with `pose review conclude`.
166	
167	### Residual risks
168	- A reviewer that does not read the brief still writes a draft the preflight refuses; the refusal names each broken rule.
169	- The reviewer runs the required plan tools and reads the code; it does not rerun the tests, which it takes from the sealed evidence.
170	
171	### Follow-ups
172	
173	- [open] Give the Claude reviewer a `sandboxed`-equivalent profile with the operating-system sandbox of Claude Code (`--settings` with `sandbox.enabled`), once `socat` is installed on the machine that runs reviews, and have the profile refuse to launch when the sandbox reports its dependencies missing, so that `go test` can be allowed again. (owner:@pose-maintainers crit:medium review:2027-01-08)
174	- [open] Extend the tie of the preflight messages to the rest of what refuses a conclusion (the structural-causality and causality-closeout mapping rules, the finding-decision rules, the reuse rules, the round protocol and `ParseReviewDraft`), and state in the brief the rules found there: three or more mappings on one basis with one pasted rationale, a basis that reaches no requirement, a draft whose outside `decision:` line disagrees with its block. (owner:@pose-maintainers crit:low review:2027-01-08)
175	- [open] Let `pose review conclude --dry-run` print the preflight blockers of a run's draft before the attestation is attempted, so a reviewer round is not spent on the shape. (owner:@pose-maintainers crit:low review:2027-01-08)
176	- [open] Offer `pose delegate review` the same read-only verbs for the Codex profile as an explicit list, so both profiles state what a reviewer may run. (owner:@pose-maintainers crit:low review:2027-01-08)
